title: Explain this passage like I am 5 years old.

messages.content: Explain this passage like I am 5 years old.
messages.focus:
Chaining: Each slot points to linked list of all elements hashing to that slot. Divide-and-conquer: n elements randomly divided into m
subsets.

messages.content:
Imagine you have a big toy box (the hash table) with many smaller bins inside (slots).

When you put a toy away, you first check which bin it belongs to. If another toy is already in that bin, you don't throw it away — you just chain them together. They sit in a little line, one after another, all in the same bin.

"Divide-and-conquer" means: instead of searching through ALL your toys to find one, you split them into smaller groups. Each bin holds just a few toys. That way, finding something is much faster — you only search the one bin it's in.
